item.title: Limiting six sources of pharmaceuticals might slash mixture toxicity risk in rivers
item.content:encoded:
Nature Geoscience, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02101-2

A machine-learning model leverages 1,017 toxicity assays in three species and 24 geospatial predictors to generate high-resolution maps of toxicity from pharmaceutical mixtures in rivers worldwide. Analyses reveal that targeted management of six key sources of pharmaceuticals might substantially reduce the river areas at risk.
item.dc:title: Limiting six sources of pharmaceuticals might slash mixture toxicity risk in rivers

item.title: Curbing six key sources could halve pharmaceutical mixture exceedance in global rivers
item.content:encoded:
Nature Geoscience, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02096-w

Pharmaceutical mixture toxicity exceeds ecological thresholds in 13% of global rivers, and targeted control of key pollution sources could substantially reduce these risks, according to an assessment of pharmaceutical pollution in rivers worldwide.
